featured_reviews.name: Samira Iqbal
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is my 2nd time ordering from Tharu Sweets. Although I live in Dubai, I had someone who got the mithai for me all the way from Mumbai. The quality of their mithai is topnotch 👌🏽 I've been looking for a mithai place that makes sweets in authentic asli cow ghee since over 10 years now 😅 since I'm quite a foodie with a sweet tooth, but until I taste the motichoor laddoo from Tharu, every other place has been a disappointment. Tharu mithai is the real deal, you can literally taste the ghee and all the mithai is fresh and tastes delish. I've ordered a variety of their sweets- motichoor laddoo, kesar katli, besan laddoo, sohan halwa, mahn ka laddoo and some others that I liked the description of but I forget their names 😂
My only issue is that their online ordering is a bit slow and won't accept international debit cards or even the Indian Bank cards. I had to use my aunt's Indian Bank account to do an online direct transfer.
Final thoughts, I definitely recommend this place for good quality mithai and pricing is reasonable.

featured_reviews.name: Jianna Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Its always been a favorite amongst my family. They have the best of Pure Ghee Sweets.. around here. Its gotten even better since a few years now. They have airconditioned their shop... and their level of hygeine has gone up tremendously too. Sweet and Savoury... all their goodies are great.. but do note that.. the prices are steep too.
The Dal Pakhwan is to die for.. seriously scrumptious..!!
And then their Alu Tikki and chholey is yum too.
Been there since so many years now... but this was the first time that I tasted.. and then bought Mysuru Paak. Its simply the melt in the mouth variant. I have tried it at so many South Indian and Maharashtrian sweet shops... but this is by far the best I've had till date.

Must mention Motichoor Laddoo too. After having the laddoo from regular local mishtaan bhandars here... I had started to hate it.
But Tharu's laddoo.. took me back in time.. straight to the halwai shops at Chowk in Allahabad.. now.. Prayagraj. Fried in Pure ghee and steeped in syrup.. yet one can feel each boondi coming apart in every bite. Rarely does one come across.. such perfectly made laddoos nowadays. Well Tharu's motichoor ladoo.. was almost there. Real Motichoor..!!
You must try.. if you havent already.

Must keep something for my next review. So adieu folks. More after my next visit there..

featured_reviews.review_text:
As one enters the shop everything looks very clean and organised. The staff is well trained in informing about their history, exchanging pleasantries and manages to put up a smile but what actually matters is their Mithais that they are selling which are not fresh!!!

This was the first time I bought an Ice Halwa, varieties of Pedas (white & brown) and some khakharas. They don't provide any sample tasting of their Mithais. Later upon the manager's intervention I was given a small sample of their brown peda which was fresh but not the other white peda or the Ice Halwa... I found that odd but went ahead on the trust of their rich legacy which was told to me by their staff... This was the first red flag.

Even though the staff knew that the sweets have gone stale they still sold it to me.  Upon tasting, I found out the truth about their stale mithai and also found out that they had not provided me with an invoice :-( Second red flag.

Now as I join the dots and it all makes sense that they probably have got good at clearing their stale products off the shelf and making money...
This was not experience that I had hoped for...

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had these delivered in Mumbai and brought over to Malaysia within 24hrs. They lasted the entire journey intact and lip smacking good!

I strongly recommend the Cheat Box, Assorted Mithai Box and Kalakand (any flavour of the Kalakand if you can get your hands on some). Bite-sized portions, provided you exercise control, which is impossible I'd say. Their namkeens are addictive, those should come with warning labels. All edibles are have allergens labelled on their packaging; it simplifies matters for those who have restrictive diets.

None of the sweets are overly sweet despite being 'sweets'. I'm not sure how to explain the irony of that sentence, but those who have an indulgent sweet tooth AND a hawk's eye on their calorie intake, you know what I mean.

Always a good experience shopping from you!

featured_reviews.name: DV
featured_reviews.review_text: This is Bori or Bora Mohalla located in South Mumbai in between Grant road and Charni road;near about Bhendi Bazaar. It is bustling with non vegetarian fast food served by many famous and age old jaunts like Tawakkal, Surti Handi, Haji tikka and many such. You can get a hot, frsh chicken tikka roll for as less as 90/- Rupees, Baida Roti for 100/- Rs. and Kababs for 140/- Rs. The dishes here are authentic Mughlai and hugely recommended. There is a variety of Muslim sweets available at Tawaqqal and some other outlets too. Some jaunts offer seating as well for couples and families. It is a feast to savour at these outlets during Ramzan.

The bheja tawa fry was rich and tasty, perfect with lemon. Didn't disappoint. Their rumali roti is soft and perfect btw.

Overall a decent place, they just need to work on the quantity of their food and the way they serve nalli.
